subject: Add the dedicated developer-edition SQL service provider with startup-state restore and blocked reporting
description:
WHY: loomrefinements.md §Provider choice and dormant state; acceptance scenario "Service provider: startup state restored; wrong service and missing permissions cause no mutation".

GROUNDING: this host has no MSSQL* service and no `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Microsoft SQL Server\Instance Names\SQL` key (measured 2026-10-03 11:49:26Z, AMC-D-PF3XTNPM, user allianzde). The provider cannot be qualified here, and the release reports it unqualified per decision 6c.

CHANGE:
- Provider abstraction: localdb | developer-service, mapped to trusted local configuration. No arbitrary endpoint, no connection string.
- The dedicated service is named explicitly and normally has Manual startup.
- A Disabled service changes startup mode only under an explicitly pre-authorized policy, and is restored after the run.
- Without that authority, or without service permission, the provider reports blocked.
- An already running service is never taken over: refuse acquisition and report it.
- Never alter startup silently, install SQL or request elevation.
- Tests use a fake service controller for the decision logic only: wrong service, missing permission, running service, Disabled without policy. Each asserts that no mutation call was made. Real-service evidence stays unqualified on this host.

AREA TESTS: npm run build; node --test --test-concurrency=1 packages/qualification/dist/test/framework.test.js; node --test --test-concurrency=1 packages/qualification/dist/test/lifecycle.test.js.
WORKER: loom-worker (Sonnet 5, effort high, as its definition sets), resumed across its milestone while its context allows (task 1, warm reuse); Opus at xhigh only through `ledger escalate <task>` when the task proves complex, meaning an unresolved design question or a defect the worker cannot land (owner rule: prefer Sonnet; Opus xhigh only for complex work).
